candidates.summary: Rocket Money/Truebill-style success-fee pricing on VERIFIED savings: free dashboard, and Runway charges a capped share (e.g. 20-35% of first-year annualized savings) only after verifySavings confirms a cancelled or downgraded charge actually stopped. This is an alternative to a flat $49-149/mo seat.
candidates.hypothesis: Bank-native verification (G1, already shipped) makes a no-savings-no-fee model safe for a startup tool, as Rocket Money's 35-60% success fee is for consumer bills. On synthetic cohorts, the expected fee per company exceeds a flat $49/mo plan while keeping false-positive billing (a fee charged on savings that did not land) under 2%.
candidates.mve: Write a script over generateDemoCompany for seeds 1..200 x {clean,noisy}. For each company, mark every planted waste item as acted-on at a random month, then run verifySavings at asOf+3 months. In a random 20% of companies, inject adversarial continuations: the cancelled vendor keeps billing under a renamed descriptor, moves to an annual cycle, or is refunded and re-billed. Report the median and p90 first-year fee at 20/35% against a $49/mo x 12 flat plan, and the false-verified rate, i.e. a fee charged while the money is still leaving. Kill the idea if the false-verified rate is above 2%, or if the median fee is below $588/yr at 35%.
evidence: research_notes/Runway product go to market/retention_features.md (sec 3: verification as pricing anchor; no competitor found shipping it)

candidates.summary: A QuickBooks ProAdvisor / QBO Accountant-style free advisor console for fractional CFOs and accountants. It gives a multi-client triage list ranked by risk: runway under N months, a burn spike, renewals due in 14 days, open waste in dollars, and unverified savings. The console is free to the advisor, and clients are billed at wholesale per-client pricing with a revenue share, plus a find-an-advisor directory later.
candidates.hypothesis: One free seat for an advisor who serves 10-30 startups brings in many paying companies (G3). ProAdvisor's free console, revenue share and lead directory (Intuit reports about 17K leads a month) is the proven template, and no bank-native equivalent exists. It works only if the triage ranking reliably surfaces the clients who need attention, so advisors return weekly.
candidates.mve: Build a cohort of 30 synthetic clients from generateDemoCompany seeds, and post-transform them to vary shape: scale the opening cash by 0.3-3x, drop or plant waste, and shift revenue growth. Record ground-truth 'needs attention' labels (runway under 6 months, a planted burn spike, an annual renewal within 14 days). Implement a pure rankClients() from the existing runway, changes and renewals libs. Measure precision@5 and recall@10 against the labels, and wall time for all 30 clients (target under 1 s). The idea is falsified if precision@5 is below 0.8, or if the ranking is no better than sorting by runway alone. Also desk-check that the RLS schema (org_id on every table) supports an advisor role reading many orgs without a schema rewrite.
evidence: research_notes/Runway product go to market/competitors.md (sec 4-5: Fathom per-client pricing, portfolio-view gap)

candidates.summary: Copilot Money/Mint-style categorization rules that stick. A founder fixes one transaction ('this is a one-off', 'this vendor is payroll', 'exclude investment proceeds'). The fix becomes a per-tenant rule that retroactively recategorizes past matches and applies to future ones before the vendor catalog or the LLM. Burn and runway update live, and the fix is shown as a correction, not hidden.
candidates.hypothesis: In consumer finance apps, user-authored rules are both a trust fix and switching cost: Copilot's name rules recategorize every past match, and Mercury Insights lets users exclude one-offs. For Runway, a handful of rule-level corrections should fix most of the dollar-weighted miscategorization on unfamiliar ledgers (G6). Per-transaction fixes would take an order of magnitude more clicks to reach the same runway accuracy.
candidates.mve: Stress the generator for G6: use noisy mode, rename 30% of vendor descriptors to strings outside the catalog, and inject one-off investment proceeds and a mislabeled payroll vendor. Run this over 100 seeds. Use DEMO_CATEGORY_LABELS as an oracle and let a simulated user fix, each turn, the highest-dollar wrong item, first as a single-transaction fix and then as a descriptor rule with retroactive propagation. Plot net-burn and runway error (months) against the number of corrections. Falsifiable thresholds: rules reach under 0.1 months of runway error in 5 or fewer corrections at the median, and per-transaction fixes need at least 5x more. If the uncorrected runway error is already under 0.1 months, the feature has low value and should be dropped.
evidence: README.md (Known limitations: categorization corrections that stick not built; detectors tuned on own generator)

candidates.summary: A HubSpot Website Grader / Ramp savings-calculator-style free 'Runway Grader' that needs no signup. The founder drops a CSV export from Rho, Mercury, Brex or a generic bank, and the deterministic pipeline runs entirely in the browser with no upload. It returns runway, the P10-P90 range, a waste score and the top 3 findings. The call to action is 'connect read-only for the weekly digest and verified savings'.
candidates.hypothesis: Activation friction from the bank-connect step (G4) and Rho-only reach cap the top of funnel. A client-side CSV grader brings time-to-first-insight to seconds for any bank's customers, including Mercury's ~300K, without OAuth or partner approval. That works only if CSV-derived findings match the API path closely enough to be credible.
candidates.mve: Export each generateDemoCompany (seeds 1..50, clean and noisy) to 3 CSV layouts: Rho-like, Mercury-like (taken from Mercury's documented export columns, by desk check) and a generic date/description/amount layout with no account or cardholder fields. Write a parser that maps them into the existing pipeline. Compare findings with the native Rho-format path: per-detector precision/recall, runway delta in months, and analysis time. Falsified if the generic layout loses more than 10 points of recall (idle-card detection is expected to degrade without cardholder data, so quantify this) or if the runway delta exceeds 0.25 months. Also verify by build-time check that the grader route makes no network calls under the existing CSP.
evidence: research_notes/Runway product go to market/retention_features.md (Mercury read-only token, ~300K customers)

candidates.summary: A Visible.vc-style two-sided investor loop. The existing investor-update generator also publishes a signed, aggregate-only 'live runway card' link (cash, burn, runway band, default-alive, verified savings; no transactions). Investors who receive it get a free portfolio page that collects every card shared with them, and can nudge other portfolio founders to connect.
candidates.hypothesis: Visible grew through founders sending updates to about 57 recipients each and pulling metrics automatically. Investors become a distribution channel when the artifact they receive is live and aggregable, not a static email. A bank-fed, deterministic card should be accurate enough, and private enough, for founders to share by default (G7).
candidates.mve: Prototype buildRunwayCard(analysis) that emits signed JSON, plus aggregatePortfolio(cards[]). Run over 40 synthetic companies (seeds, with cash and revenue scaled to vary runway). Checks: (1) every card figure equals the dashboard/investor-update figure exactly (0 mismatches); (2) a privacy test that no vendor name, cardholder name, transaction id or amount under the card's rounding threshold appears in the payload; (3) tamper detection, so that editing any field fails verification; (4) the portfolio view sorts the companies that truly have under 6 months of runway into the top quintile. Falsified if any figure mismatches or any transaction-level leak occurs. Note that whether recipients actually adopt it cannot be tested in this sandbox.
evidence: research_notes/Runway product go to market/retention_features.md (Visible 57 recipients avg; ChartMogul integration drove stickiness)
